answer: In node2vec, p controls how likely the walk is to immediately return to the previous node, and q controls whether the walk behaves more like a breadth-first search (BFS) or a depth-first search (DFS). On BlogCatalog, performance improving as both p and q increase suggests that the best embeddings come from walks that are less “sticky” and less strongly biased toward local neighborhoods. In other words, the model benefits from exploring farther away and sampling a broader, more diverse set of nodes rather than repeatedly revisiting nearby ones. This implies that BlogCatalog’s useful structural signals are captured better by more exploratory, less locally constrained random walks, so node2vec’s walk strategy there is closer to a more global/DFS-like exploration than a tight neighborhood-preserving BFS-like one.
